ww.Vasodilation and more filtration: Reduced, not increased, sympathetic stimulation causes vasodilation at rest.
ww.No change in GFR: GFR is very sensitive to small changes in afferent arteriolar pressure and tone.

evidence: When the frequency of action potentials increases, the arteriolar smooth muscle constricts (vasoconstriction), resulting in diminished glomerular flow, so less filtration occurs.

tp: Because the margin is so small, tiny changes in afferent arterial pressure can change GFR significantly.

ww.About 40 mm Hg: The required differential is much smaller.
ww.About 100 mm Hg: The required differential is much smaller.

evidence: Only a 10 mm Hg pressure differential across the glomerulus is required for normal GFR, so very small changes in afferent arterial pressure significantly increase or decrease GFR.

bw: Afferent arteriole stretched by rising pressure
tp: When pressure drops, the same smooth muscle relaxes and flow stays even.

ww.Tubuloglomerular feedback: This acts through the macula densa and paracrine signals, not stretch of the arteriole.
ww.Renin-angiotensin mechanism: This is a hormonal mechanism, not an intrinsic stretch response.

evidence: The myogenic mechanism regulating blood flow within the kidney depends upon a characteristic shared by most smooth muscle cells of the body.

tp: Macula densa cells are part of the juxtaglomerular apparatus and drive tubuloglomerular feedback.

ww.Juxtaglomerular cells: JG cells are in the afferent arteriole wall and secrete renin.

evidence: Specialized macula densa cells in this segment of the tubule respond to changes in the fluid flow rate and Na+ concentration.

bw: More NaCl reaches the macula densa
tp: Constriction slows blood flow and reduces GFR. When GFR falls, ATP and adenosine fall and the afferent arteriole dilates.

ww.The efferent arteriole dilates: The feedback in the source acts on the afferent arteriole.

evidence: ATP and adenosine act locally as paracrine factors to stimulate the myogenic juxtaglomerular cells of the afferent arteriole to constrict, slowing blood flow and reducing GFR.

bw: Paracrine signal that relaxes the afferent arteriole
Fine-tunes the effect of ATP and adenosine
tp: NO relaxes the afferent arteriole at the same time ATP and adenosine make it contract.
evidence: Thus, NO fine-tunes the effects of adenosine and ATP on GFR.
